dollar5_test.why: this duration's recorder preserved the touch prices but not the level sizes, and the $5 rule requires displayed depth for the WHOLE quantity. Running it against an assumed size would fabricate the fill, so it is reported untestable and moved to forward shadow collection.

favorite_test.note: requires BOTH sides executable so the favorite is identified from a real two-sided book, which is why n is far smaller than the underdog matrix

structural_cost.why_it_matters: a taker pays half this spread on entry. When the two executable asks sum materially above 1.00, no directional taker bet on either side can be positive on average: the excess IS the cost, and it is charged before any view.

dollar5_test.sizing_rule: q = ceil(5 / ((1-p)*(1-0.07p))); a deterministic function of entry price alone. No martingale, no size increase after a loss.

execution_discipline: executable ask only. UP pays the YES ask; DOWN pays 1 - the YES bid and consumes the bid ladder. No midpoint, no last trade, no UI probability, no touch-beyond-size, no queue assumption, no future quote, no post-settlement reference as an entry feature.
